question: What is the primary relationship between a Class and an Object in Dart?
options: A class is a blueprint or template, while an object is a concrete instance created from that blueprint
An object is the blueprint, while a class is an individual instance in memory
Classes and objects are identical terms and can be used interchangeably in Dart
A class is a function, while an object is a primitive data type
explanation: A class defines the structure (properties) and behavior (methods), while an object is an actual instance created in memory from that blueprint.

question: When does a constructor execute in Dart?
options: Automatically at the exact moment a new object is created
Only when explicitly invoked using a dot operator like `myObject.constructor()`
Whenever any method inside the class finishes execution
Only when the program terminates to clean up memory
explanation: A constructor is a special function whose name matches the class. It automatically executes whenever `ClassName()` is called to create and initialize a new object.

question: What happens if you define a custom parameterized constructor in a Dart class without declaring an unnamed no-argument constructor?
options: Dart no longer provides the implicit default no-argument constructor
Dart keeps the default no-argument constructor available alongside the custom one
Dart generates a compile-time error unless an empty constructor is also written
Dart automatically converts the parameterized constructor into a named constructor
explanation: Dart only provides an implicit default constructor `ClassName()` if NO constructors are declared. Declaring any custom constructor eliminates the automatic default constructor.

question: What is the primary purpose of the `this` keyword inside a Dart class?
options: It refers to the current object instance, disambiguating instance fields from parameter variables of the same name
It imports external Dart libraries into the class definition
It converts an instance method into a static class-level method
It marks an instance variable as immutable and prevents reassignment
explanation: `this` points to the current object instance. For example, `this.name = name;` assigns the incoming parameter `name` to the instance property `this.name`.

question: Which Dart feature allows a single class to provide multiple alternative creation paths (e.g., `Student.guest()`)?
options: Named constructors
Static inheritance
Cascade assignment
Spread arguments
explanation: Dart does not support constructor overloading by parameter signature. Instead, Dart provides Named Constructors (syntax: `ClassName.identifier()`) to allow multiple distinct constructors.

question: How do you access a getter like `double get area => width * height;` on an object `rect`?
options: As a property without parentheses: `print(rect.area);`
As a standard method call with parentheses: `print(rect.area());`
Using the get keyword: `print(rect.get.area);`
Using double colons: `print(Rectangle::area);`
explanation: Getters in Dart are accessed using standard property syntax without parentheses (`rect.area`), allowing calculated values to be read like ordinary fields.

question: Which statement correctly describes a Dart setter?
options: It is defined using `set`, has no explicit return type, and is invoked via assignment: `obj.property = value;`
It must return a boolean indicating whether the update was successful
It is called like a method: `obj.setProperty(value);`
It can only be used on static class variables
explanation: Setters are declared using `set setterName(Type value)` without a return type, and callers assign to them using property assignment syntax.

question: How are `static` variables and methods different from instance variables and methods?
options: Static members belong to the class itself and are accessed via `ClassName.member`, not through an individual object instance
Static members can only be used inside the `main()` function
Static variables change their value automatically whenever an object is destroyed
Instance methods cannot access instance variables, whereas static methods can
explanation: Static variables and methods belong to the class itself. Only one shared copy exists across all instances, accessed directly via the class name (e.g. `Student.college`).

question: What is required to declare a `const` constructor in Dart?
options: The constructor must use the `const` prefix and all instance fields in the class must be declared as `final`
All methods in the class must return constant strings or numbers
The class must not have any properties
All constructor parameters must be optional integers
explanation: To define a `const` constructor, the constructor must be prefixed with `const`, and every instance variable in the class must be marked `final`.

question: If `Student s1 = Student('Rahul');` and `Student s2 = Student('Rahul');`, what does `identical(s1, s2)` return?
options: `false`, because they are two separate objects located at different memory addresses
`true`, because all their field values are identical
`null`, because `identical()` is only valid on numbers
A compile-time type mismatch error
explanation: `identical()` checks reference equality (memory identity). Since `s1` and `s2` were created by two separate constructor calls, they reside at different memory addresses, returning `false`.
